mainTopic: משה's bold prayers for Israel after the עגל and the מרגלים, and the rule to praise God before making requests.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof that God Himself admits a role in Israel's failings. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says three פסוקים like this keep Israel standing, and רב פפא adds a more direct one. Next, רבי אלעזר and דבי רבי ינאי teach that משה spoke boldly to God, blaming the abundance of gold ('ודי זהב') for the עגל. A series of משלים and פסוקים back this up: too much good leads to sin, and God Himself later agreed. The גמרא then follows משה's prayers after the עגל: 'לך רד', 'הרף ממני', his refusal to become a new nation, and many readings of the word 'וַיְחַל'. It continues with משה's arguments from God's eternal oath and from what the nations would say after the מרגלים, ending with God's 'סלחתי כדבריך'. Finally, רבי שמלאי learns from משה that one should praise God before asking for one's needs. The amud closes with a memory list for the teachings that come next.

steps.title: God Himself admits a role in Israel's sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes a proof from the previous lines by quoting the פסוק in מיכה where God says 'those I have dealt badly with.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And those whom I have dealt badly with.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof it started just before this point. It quotes a פסוק in which God speaks about Israel as 'those whom I have dealt badly with.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the words 'הרעתי', God speaks about Himself as the one who caused the harm. This shows that God Himself admits He had a part in Israel's going wrong. That idea sets up רבי חמא's teaching in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written; introduces a פסוק as a source
I have dealt badly with, I caused harm (God speaking about Himself)

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And those whom I have dealt badly with.'
phrases.notes: מיכה 4:6

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun right before this point.
steps.raayaObject: That God Himself admitted He had a part in Israel's sin.

steps.title: Without three verses, Israel could not stand
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says that if not for three פסוקים, Israel would collapse under judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: If not for these three פסוקים, the legs of the enemies of Israel would have given way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא makes a new statement: three פסוקים are what keep Israel standing. The גמרא will list the three in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If Israel carried the full blame for every sin, it could not survive God's judgment. Three פסוקים show that God also has a hand in a person's heart, and that gives Israel a defense. 'The enemies of Israel' is a polite way of talking about Israel itself.

keyTerms.meaning: If not for, were it not for
Literally 'enemies of Israel'; a polite way to refer to Israel itself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'שונאי ישראל' as real enemies. The גמרא doesn't want to say something bad about Israel directly, so it puts the bad words on 'their enemies.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥama son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:
If not for these three verses,
the legs of the enemies of Israel would have collapsed.
phrases.notes: He really means Israel itself; the גמרא just avoids saying something bad about Israel directly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that God shares a role in Israel's sin and widens it to three פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three פסוקים showing God's role in the human heart are what allow Israel to survive judgment.

steps.title: Listing the three verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the three פסוקים: ואשר הרעתי, the clay in the potter's hand, and the removal of the heart of stone.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is 'And those whom I have dealt badly with.' One is 'Like clay in the potter's hand, so are you in My hand, house of Israel.' And one is 'I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly which three פסוקים רבי חמא was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק shows God shaping Israel's heart or actions. The first shows God admitting a role in their sin. The second compares Israel to clay that the potter shapes. The third shows God Himself changing a hard heart into a soft one.

keyTerms.meaning: One (Aramaic); used here to count the פסוקים
Heart of stone, a hard heart
Heart of flesh, a soft and open heart

phrases.english: One, as it is written: 'And those whom I have dealt badly with,'
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק from מיכה quoted in step 1.

phrases.english: and one, as it is written:
'Behold, like clay in the potter's hand,'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 18:6

phrases.english: so are you in My hand, house of Israel,'
and one, as it is written:
'And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh,'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 36:26

phrases.english: and I will give you a heart of flesh.'

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the three פסוקים that רבי חמא mentioned.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חמא's claim that three פסוקים protect Israel.
steps.whatToRemember: The three פסוקים: ואשר הרעתי, clay in the potter's hand, and the heart of stone replaced by a heart of flesh.

steps.title: A different, more direct verse
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings a different source: God says He will cause Israel to walk in His laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is from here: 'And I will put My spirit within you, and I will cause you to walk in My laws.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers his own source for the same idea, a פסוק from a little later in the same chapter of יחזקאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this פסוק, God says directly that He will make Israel follow His laws. So God's part in Israel's behavior is stated outright, not just hinted at. This gives a clearer source for the same point.

keyTerms.meaning: From here; introduces a different source
And I will cause, I will make it happen

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's פסוק says it most directly: God Himself makes Israel walk in His laws.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: From here:
'And I will put My spirit within you,'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 36:27

phrases.english: and I will cause you to walk in My laws.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the idea in רבי חמא's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The source for God's role in Israel's behavior is יחזקאל 36:27, where God says He will cause Israel to walk in His laws.

steps.title: משה spoke harshly toward Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that משה spoke boldly toward God, reading 'אל ה׳' as 'על ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: משה spoke harsh words toward Heaven. The פסוק says 'And משה prayed to ה׳.' Do not read it as 'to ה׳.' Read it as 'against ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר adds משה to the list of people who spoke boldly toward God. He proves it by reading one word of a פסוק differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק simply says משה prayed 'אֶל' (to) ה׳‎. רבי אלעזר re-reads the word as 'עַל' (against, or upon), which shows a forceful, demanding tone. The next step explains why this kind of re-reading is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as... (a way of drawing a lesson by reading a word differently)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אַל תִּקְרֵי' does not mean the פסוק is written wrong. The written text stays the same, and the different reading is used to draw out an extra lesson.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Moshe spoke harsh words toward Heaven.
As it says: "And Moshe prayed to ה׳"
phrases.notes: במדבר 11:2

phrases.english: Do not read "to ה׳,"
but rather "against ה׳."
phrases.notes: עַל can mean 'upon' or 'against,' so it hints that משה spoke forcefully toward God.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מֹשֶׁה הֵטִיחַ דְּבָרִים כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of bold words toward God, now about משה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה spoke boldly toward Heaven, as shown by reading 'אל ה׳' as 'על ה׳'.

steps.title: Why אלף and עין can be swapped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the reading 'על' for 'אל': the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב swapped these two letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works because the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב would read an אלף as an עין, and an עין as an אלף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it is fair to read אֶל as עַל. In one school these two letters sounded alike and were used in place of each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אֶל is spelled with an אלף and עַל with an עין. Since the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב treated the two letters as interchangeable, changing one word into the other is a reasonable reading and not a random guess.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of, the students of

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: For in the school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov
they would read alefs as ayins,
and ayins as alefs.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁכֵּן דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the 'אל תקרי' reading of step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The swap of אֶל for עַל in step 5
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reading habit of the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

steps.title: A different source: "ודי זהב"
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ינאי prove that משה spoke boldly toward God from the words 'ודי זהב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי say: we learn it from here, from the words 'and Di Zahav.'
steps.whatsHappening: A different school brings its own source for the idea that משה spoke boldly toward God. This step sets up a question about what the words mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of re-reading 'אל ה׳', דבי רבי ינאי point to 'ודי זהב' in a list of places at the start of ספר דברים. The meaning of these words is not yet explained, so the next step will ask about it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And Di Zahav,' a name in the list of places in דברים 1:1

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say:
From here: "And Di Zahav."
phrases.notes: דברים 1:1

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמְרִי, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for רבי אלעזר's idea in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That משה spoke boldly toward God

steps.title: What does "ודי זהב" mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how 'ודי זהב' shows that משה spoke boldly.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and Di Zahav' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the words 'ודי זהב' mean. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface 'ודי זהב' looks like just a place name. The question asks how it could hint at bold words from משה.

phrases.english: What is "and Di Zahav"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וְדִי זָהָב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the source brought in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the words 'ודי זהב' show that משה spoke boldly toward God

steps.title: משה blames the gold for the Golden Calf
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ינאי explain that משה told God that the huge amount of gold He gave Israel, until they said 'די', is what caused the עגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: This is what משה said before the הקב״ה: Master of the World, the silver and gold that You showered on Israel, until they said 'Enough!', is what caused them to make the Calf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains 'ודי זהב' as 'so much gold that they said די (enough).' משה used this to defend Israel after the עגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word די is read as 'enough,' and זהב is the gold. משה argued that God's own generous gift of wealth led to the sin, which is a bold thing to say to God. This shows how משה spoke boldly toward Heaven to defend Israel.

keyTerms.meaning: You showered, gave in great amounts

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי אלעזר and דבי רבי ינאי teach that משה spoke boldly toward God. One learns it from 'על ה׳' and the other from 'ודי זהב', where משה blamed the abundance of gold for the עגל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This fits the larger theme of the סוגיא: great people defended Israel by speaking forcefully to God, and their words were accepted.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: This is what Moshe said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,
because of the silver and gold
that You showered upon Israel,
until they said "Enough"
phrases.notes: This is the 'די' of 'די זהב': there was so much gold that they said 'enough.'

phrases.english: that is what caused them to make the Calf.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: כָּךְ אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ודי זהב' means that the gold God gave until Israel said 'די' is what caused the עגל, which was משה's bold defense of Israel.

steps.title: A lion roars over meat, not straw
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ינאי give a משל: a lion only roars when it stands over meat, not over straw.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: A lion does not roar over a basket of straw, only over a basket of meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The school of רבי ינאי adds a short picture to back up משה's claim from the previous step. A lion only gets loud and wild when it has meat, which is something good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, משה argued that the abundance of gold is what caused the עגל. This משל supports that idea: a creature acts out when it has plenty, not when it has nothing. So Israel's sin came from having too much, not from lacking.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
A lion does not roar
over a basket of straw,
but only over a basket of meat.
phrases.notes: The idea is that the lion gets wild only when it has something good to enjoy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמרי דבי רבי ינאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 9's claim with a משל.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that abundance of gold caused the sin of the עגל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משל of a lion that roars only over meat

steps.title: The cow that kicked after eating good food
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא compares Israel to a thin cow that was fed fine food and then kicked its owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: It is like a man who had a thin but big-boned cow. He fed it lupines, a fine food, and it started kicking him. He said to it: What made you kick me, if not the lupines I fed you?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא gives a second משל for the same idea. The owner fed his cow well, and the good food is exactly what made it rebellious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משל is closer to משה's argument than the lion: here the owner himself gave the good thing. Just as the owner admits his own feeding caused the kicking, God's gift of gold is what led Israel to the עגל.

keyTerms.meaning: Lupines or vetch, a rich animal feed

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
It is like a person who had
a thin cow with large limbs.
He fed it lupines,
and it started kicking him.
He said to it: Who caused you
to kick me?
Nothing but the lupines that I fed you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי אושעיא משל לאדם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second משל for the same idea as step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that God's generous gift led Israel to sin
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משל of a cow that kicked after being fed rich food

steps.title: The pampered son placed at a bad doorway
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן compares Israel to a son whose father pampered him, gave him money, and sat him at the door of a brothel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is like a man who had a son. He bathed him, anointed him with oil, fed him, gave him drink, hung a purse of money on his neck, and sat him at the entrance of a brothel. What can that son do not to sin?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a third משל that is even stronger. The father did everything to set his son up for sin, so how could the son avoid it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the father not only gives good things but also puts the son right in front of temptation. This matches משה's bold defense: God gave Israel so much that sinning was almost expected, which lessens their blame.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מָשָׁל לְאָדָם אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ בֵּן.
phrases.english: It is like a person who had a son.
He bathed him and anointed him,
fed him and gave him drink,
and hung a purse around his neck,
and sat him at the entrance of a brothel.

phrases.aramaic: מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ הַבֵּן שֶׁלֹּא יֶחֱטָא?!
phrases.english: What can that son do not to sin?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן משל לאדם אחד שהיה לו בן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, stronger משל for the same idea.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that God's generosity set up the conditions for the עגל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משל of a pampered son placed at a brothel's door

steps.title: A popular saying and a פסוק: a full belly leads to sin
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת quotes a common saying that a full stomach leads to evil, and supports it with a פסוק in הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב הונא said in the name of רב ששת: This is what people say: A full belly leads to all kinds of evil. As it says: 'When they were fed, they were full; they were full, and their heart grew proud; so they forgot Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת moves from משלים to a well-known saying and then to a פסוק. Both show that being full and satisfied leads to sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we had only comparisons. Now the idea gets support from a פסוק: eating and being full led to pride, and pride led to forgetting God. This gives the idea a source in תנ״ך.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say, a common saying

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Huna said
that Rav Sheshet said:
This is what people say:
A full belly leads to all kinds of evil.
As it says: 'When they were fed, they were full;'
phrases.notes: הושע 13:6

phrases.english: they were full, and their heart grew proud;
therefore they forgot Me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: היינו דאמרי אינשי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from משלים to a saying and a פסוק for the same idea.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that being full and satisfied leads to sin

steps.title: רב נחמן brings a different פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the source for this idea is a פסוק in דברים about a proud heart forgetting God.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The source is from here: 'And your heart will grow proud, and you will forget ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן agrees with the idea but gives a different פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea itself is not argued about here. The only question is which פסוק shows it best, and רב נחמן prefers one from the תורה, in דברים, over the one from הושע.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, introducing a different source
And your heart will grow proud

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: From here:
'And your heart will grow proud, and you will forget ה׳.'
phrases.notes: דברים 8:14

steps.triggerLanguage: רב נחמן אמר מהכא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the same idea as step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that being full and satisfied leads to sin

steps.title: The רבנן bring a third פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן give another source: a פסוק in דברים about eating, being full, growing fat, and turning away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: The source is from here: 'And they will eat and be full and grow fat, and turn away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן give a third פסוק for the same idea. It lists eating, being full, and growing fat, followed by turning away to other gods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק shows the whole chain in one place: eating leads to fullness, fullness to comfort, and comfort to turning away from God. The next step adds one more possible source.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority of the rabbis

steps.whatToRemember: The משלים and פסוקים all teach one point: too much good and comfort can lead a person to sin. That is the basis for משה's bold defense of Israel after the עגל.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: From here:
'And they will eat and be full and grow fat, and turn away.'
phrases.notes: דברים 31:20. The פסוק continues: they turn to other gods.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבנן אמרי מהכא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third פסוק for the same idea, closing the list.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that being full and satisfied leads to sin

steps.title: One more source: ישורון grew fat and kicked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a final פסוק showing that being full and comfortable leads to rebelling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, learn it from this פסוק: 'And ישורון grew fat and kicked.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more possible source for the idea that a full stomach leads to sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 14 and 15 already gave פסוקים from דברים (8:14 and 31:20). This is one more, shorter option, from שירת האזינו (דברים 32:15). Here 'kicking' is the picture of rebelling after being well fed.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: an introduction to another option
A poetic name for the Jewish people
And he kicked, meaning he rebelled

phrases.english: And if you want, say it is learned from here:
"And Yeshurun grew fat and kicked."
phrases.notes: דברים 32:15

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another source for the same idea as Steps 14-15.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that being full and comfortable leads to rebellion

steps.title: God agreed with משה that the gold caused the sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן brings a פסוק showing that הקדוש ברוך הוא admitted that the riches He gave Israel led to idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: How do we know that הקדוש ברוך הוא came around and agreed with משה? Because it says: 'I gave them lots of silver, and gold, which they used for the בעל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself agreed with משה's defense of Israel: the wealth was what led them to sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא, משה argued that the gold was to blame. Here the פסוק in הושע has God Himself saying 'I gave them silver and gold, and they made a בעל from it.' That reads as God admitting משה's point.

keyTerms.meaning: An idol worshipped by other nations

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, came around
and agreed with Moshe?
phrases.notes: He agreed with what משה argued earlier: that all the gold Israel had is what led them to sin.

phrases.english: As it says:
"And I gave them a lot of silver,
and gold, which they made into the בעל."
phrases.notes: הושע 2:10

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן שֶׁחָזַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְהוֹדָה לוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the theme of wealth causing sin by showing that God accepted משה's argument.
steps.raayaObject: That הקדוש ברוך הוא agreed with משה that wealth caused the sin
steps.raayaSupportSource: הושע 2:10, 'וכסף הרביתי להם וזהב עשו לבעל'
steps.whatToRemember: The whole section ends with God Himself agreeing that too much wealth brought Israel to sin. That gives weight to משה's defense of them.

steps.title: What does 'Go, descend' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק where God tells משה 'לך רד' and asks what these words mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says: 'And ה׳ spoke to משה: Go, descend.' What does 'Go, descend' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about the חטא העגל by asking what 'לך רד' means. It is setting up רבי אלעזר's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was going down the mountain anyway, so the double phrase 'go, descend' seems to say something more. The גמרא wants to know what deeper message it carries.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? What does it mean?

phrases.english: "And ה׳ spoke to Moshe:
Go, descend."
phrases.notes: שמות 32:7

phrases.english: What does "go, descend" mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לֶךְ רֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the cause of the sin to what happened between God and משה after it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the words 'לך רד'

steps.title: משה, step down from your greatness
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that God told משה his greatness existed only for Israel, so now that they had sinned he had no role. משה lost his strength.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: הקדוש ברוך הוא told משה: Step down from your greatness! I only gave you greatness for the sake of Israel. Now that Israel sinned, what do I need you for? Right away משה's strength was gone, and he could not speak.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question: 'רד' means 'go down from your high position.' Hearing this, משה was crushed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Descend' is read as a drop in status, not just walking down the mountain. משה's importance came from being Israel's leader, so if Israel fell, his role fell too. This explains why משה at first could not pray for them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moshe:
Moshe, step down from your greatness!
Did I give you greatness at all
except for the sake of Israel?
And now that Israel has sinned,
what do I need you for?
Right away Moshe's strength grew weak,
and he had no strength to speak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'רד' means step down from your greatness, because משה's greatness was only for Israel's sake.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a leader's greatness comes from the people he serves.

steps.title: 'Let Me be' showed משה it depended on him
steps.stepSummary: When God said 'הרף ממני', משה understood that Israel's fate depended on him, so he got up and prayed hard for mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: But once God said 'Let Me be, and I will destroy them,' משה said: This depends on me! Right away he stood up, strengthened himself in prayer, and begged for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר continues: God's words 'let Me be' gave משה back his strength, and he started praying for Israel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only ask someone to 'let go' if he is holding you back. So משה realized that God was waiting on him, and his prayer could stop the punishment. The same God who made him weak in Step 19 now hinted that he still had power.

keyTerms.meaning: Let Me be, leave Me alone

phrases.english: But once He said
"Let Me be, and I will destroy them,"
phrases.notes: דברים 9:14

phrases.english: Moshe said:
This matter depends on me!
Right away he stood and strengthened himself in prayer,
and begged for mercy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁאָמַר הֶרֶף מִמֶּנִּי וְאַשְׁמִידֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אלעזר's words, showing how משה went from weakness back to strength.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God's words 'הרף ממני' hinted to משה that his prayer could save Israel, so he prayed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the power of תפילה: God's decree was waiting on the prayer of a צדיק.

steps.title: Parable of the king, his son, and his friend
steps.stepSummary: A משל: a king beating his son says he would kill him if not for his friend sitting there, so the friend realizes it depends on him and saves the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a king who was angry at his son and was beating him badly. The king's friend was sitting in front of him and was afraid to say anything. The king said: If not for this friend of mine sitting here, I would kill you! The friend said: This depends on me. Right away he stood up and saved him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a משל to explain what happened between God and משה in Step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king is הקדוש ברוך הוא, the son is ישראל, and the friend is משה. Like the friend, משה was first afraid to speak, until the king's own words showed him he had the power to stop it. The משל makes clear that 'הרף ממני' was really an invitation to step in.

keyTerms.meaning: His friend, someone who loves him

phrases.english: It is like a king who was angry at his son,
and was hitting him with a heavy beating.
And his friend was sitting before him,
and was afraid to say anything to him.
The king said:
If not for this friend of mine who is sitting before me,
I would have killed you.
The friend said: This matter depends on me.
Right away he stood up and saved him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל לְמֶלֶךְ שֶׁכָּעַס עַל בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates Steps 19-20 with a parable.
steps.raayaObject: That God's words 'הרף ממני' meant משה's prayer could save Israel
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משל of the king, his son, and his friend

steps.title: משה 'grabbed' God until He forgave Israel
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reads 'הניחה לי' as showing that משה held on to God, like grabbing a friend's clothing, and refused to let go until He forgave Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says: 'Now leave Me be, so My anger can burn against them and I will destroy them, and I will make you into a great nation.' רבי אבהו said: If the פסוק were not written, it would be impossible to say this. It teaches that משה grabbed hold of הקדוש ברוך הוא, like a person who grabs his friend by his clothing, and said: רבונו של עולם, I will not let You go until You forgive and pardon them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו explains a daring point in the פסוק: 'leave Me be' means משה was, so to speak, holding on to God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הניחה לי' means 'let go of Me,' which suggests משה was holding on. רבי אבהו admits this is too bold to say on our own, but the פסוק itself says it. This shows how forcefully משה prayed, which fits Steps 20-21.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave Me be, let go of Me
If the פסוק were not written

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not mean that משה physically held God, who has no body. רבי אבהו is warning that this is a picture of how intense the prayer was, and that we may only say it because the פסוק hints to it.
steps.whatToRemember: משה refused to accept the decree. His bold, persistent תפילה is the model for praying for others.

phrases.english: "And now, leave Me be,
so My anger will burn against them and I will destroy them,
and I will make you into a great nation, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות 32:10

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
If the פסוק were not written,
it would be impossible to say it.

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁתְּפָסוֹ מֹשֶׁה לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: It teaches that Moshe grabbed hold of the Holy One, Blessed be He,

phrases.aramaic: כְּאָדָם שֶׁהוּא תּוֹפֵס אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ בְּבִגְדוֹ,
phrases.english: like a person who grabs his friend by his clothing,
and he said before Him:
Master of the world,
I will not let You go
until You forgive and pardon them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אִלְמָלֵא מִקְרָא כָּתוּב אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאוֹמְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to another פסוק about the same moment and shows how forcefully משה prayed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'הניחה לי' teaches that משה, so to speak, held on to God and would not let go until He forgave Israel.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a צדיק's persistent prayer can turn away a harsh decree.

steps.title: A one-legged chair cannot stand
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains משה's answer to God's offer to make a great nation from him. If the merit of all three אבות could not hold back God's anger, his merit alone surely could not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And I will make of you a great nation.' רבי אלעזר said: משה said to God, 'Master of the world, if a chair with three legs cannot stand before You when You are angry, then a chair with one leg surely cannot!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the פסוק, God's offer to start a new nation from משה. רבי אלעזר explains why משה said no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'three legs' are the three אבות, whose merit was not enough to protect Israel from God's anger. A nation built on משה alone would rest on just one leg. So it would be even weaker, a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: A chair with three legs (the three אבות)
At the time of Your anger
All the more so (a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: משה is not saying God cannot do it. He is saying a nation that depends only on his merit would be even less protected than Israel, who has the merit of all three אבות.

phrases.english: "And I will make of you a great nation, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות 32:10

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Moshe said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
if a chair with three legs
phrases.notes: The three legs stand for the three אבות and their combined merit.

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַעֲמוֹד לְפָנֶיךָ בִּשְׁעַת כַּעְסֶךְ.
phrases.english: cannot stand before You at the time of Your anger,
a chair with one leg
phrases.notes: That's משה himself, standing on his merit alone.

phrases.english: all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי אלעזר: אמר משה לפני הקדוש ברוך הוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the same פסוק and explains משה's response to God's offer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה refused to become the founder of a new nation, because his merit alone could not withstand God's anger when the merit of the three אבות had not.

steps.title: Shame before the forefathers
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר adds a second reason. The אבות would say that משה looked for greatness for himself instead of praying for Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but I would be ashamed before my forefathers. Now they will say: 'Look at the leader He put over them! He asked for greatness for himself and did not ask for mercy for them.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר keeps going with משה's words and adds a second argument for turning down the offer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason was practical: one leg is too weak. This second reason is moral. A leader who accepts personal greatness while his people are being destroyed would be shamed before the אבות.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but (adds a further point)

phrases.english: And not only that, but
I have shame before my forefathers.
Now they will say:
See the leader that He placed over them!
He asked for greatness for himself,
and did not ask for mercy for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: ולא עוד אלא שיש בי בושת פנים מאבותי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reason to רבי אלעזר's explanation of משה's refusal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה would be shamed before the אבות if he took greatness for himself and did not pray for Israel.

steps.title: משה prayed until he became sick
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads the unusual word 'וַיְחַל' as related to sickness. משה prayed so hard that it made him ill.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And משה pleaded before God.' רבי אלעזר said: This teaches that משה stood in prayer before the Holy One, Blessed be He, until it made him sick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק, which uses the unusual word 'וַיְחַל'. רבי אלעזר gives the first of several explanations, and the next steps add more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר connects 'וַיְחַל' to the root for sickness (חולי). That shows how much effort משה put into his prayer for Israel.

keyTerms.meaning: He pleaded (an unusual word, explained in several ways)

phrases.english: "And Moshe pleaded before the Lord,"
phrases.notes: שמות 32:11

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: This teaches
that Moshe stood in prayer
before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
until it made him sick.
phrases.notes: He hears 'וַיְחַל' as sounding like the word for being sick.

steps.triggerLanguage: ויחל משה את פני ה׳ אמר רבי אלעזר מלמד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new פסוק and starts a series of explanations of the word 'וַיְחַל'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'וַיְחַל' means משה prayed until he became physically ill.

steps.title: משה got God's vow annulled
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a second reading of 'וַיְחַל'. משה prayed until God's vow to destroy Israel was annulled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: משה prayed until he annulled His vow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different explanation of the same word 'וַיְחַל'. The proof for his reading comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'sickness', רבא connects 'וַיְחַל' to the language of annulling a vow. This makes it as though God had made a vow to destroy Israel, and משה undid it.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
until he annulled His vow for Him.
phrases.notes: 'His vow' means God's vow to destroy Israel, which משה got cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבא אמר עד שהפר לו נדרו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different reading of 'וַיְחַל' alongside רבי אלעזר's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'וַיְחַל' means משה annulled God's vow to destroy Israel.

steps.title: Proof from the laws of vows
steps.stepSummary: רבא's reading is supported by the same word in the פרשה of vows, 'לֹא יַחֵל דְּבָרוֹ'. There we learn that others can annul a person's vow even though he cannot annul it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is written 'וַיְחַל', and there it is written 'He shall not break his word.' And the Master said: He himself cannot annul it, but others can annul it for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבא's reading by matching 'וַיְחַל' to the same word used for vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of vows, 'לֹא יַחֵל' teaches that a person cannot cancel his own vow, but others (a חכם or court) can cancel it for him. So 'וַיְחַל משה' means משה acted as the 'other' who annulled God's vow.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here... and it is written there (comparing a word in two places)
He shall not break his word
The Master said (quoting an earlier teaching)

phrases.english: Here it is written: "vayechal,"
and there it is written: "He shall not break his word,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 30:3

phrases.english: and the Master said:
He himself cannot annul it,
but others can annul it for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כתיב הכא ויחל וכתיב התם לא יחל דברו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind רבא's reading.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that 'וַיְחַל' refers to annulling a vow
steps.raayaSupportSource: The matching word in במדבר 30:3, 'לֹא יַחֵל דְּבָרוֹ', along with the teaching that others can annul a person's vow for him

steps.title: משה offered his life for Israel
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives a third reading of 'וַיְחַל'. משה gave himself over to death for Israel, as he said, 'Erase me from Your book.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: This teaches that משה gave himself over to death for them, as it says: 'And if not, erase me, please, from Your book.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the third explanation of 'וַיְחַל' and proves it from משה's own words later in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל links 'וַיְחַל' to the idea of death (חלל, a dead person). His proof is that משה asked to be erased from God's book if Israel was not forgiven. That shows he was ready to die for them.
steps.whatToRemember: So far the word 'וַיְחַל' has three readings, and each shows a different side of משה's devotion to Israel. רבי אלעזר says he prayed until he became sick. רבא says he got God's vow annulled. שמואל says he offered his own life. The next steps add more readings.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
This teaches that he gave himself over to death for them,
as it is stated:
"And if not, erase me, please, from Your book."
phrases.notes: שמות 32:32

steps.triggerLanguage: ושמואל אמר מלמד שמסר עצמו למיתה עליהם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third reading of 'וַיְחַל', alongside those of רבי אלעזר and רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'וַיְחַל' means משה was willing to die for Israel, as shown by his request 'מְחֵנִי נָא מִסִּפְרְךָ'.

steps.title: משה made God's mercy take effect
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of רב יצחק gives another reading of 'וַיְחַל': משה caused the מדת רחמים to rest upon Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב יצחק: The word 'וַיְחַל' teaches that משה caused God's attribute of mercy to come down upon Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more explanation of the word 'וַיְחַל' to the list of readings it has been giving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'וַיְחַל' is read like 'הֻחֲלָה', meaning 'made to take effect'. The earlier readings were about what happened to משה (sickness) or to God's vow (annulled). This one is about the result: mercy now rested on Israel.

keyTerms.meaning: That it was made to take effect, to rest upon
It teaches (introduces a lesson drawn from a word)

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Yitzchak said:
It teaches that there was made to take effect upon them
phrases.notes: 'הֻחֲלָה' shares its letters with 'וַיְחַל', and that's the whole point of this reading.

phrases.english: the attribute of mercy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהֻחֲלָה עֲלֵיהֶם מִדַּת רַחֲמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth reading of 'וַיְחַל', following שמואל's reading
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'וַיְחַל' means משה made the מדת רחמים take effect upon Israel.

steps.title: משה told God that destroying Israel is beneath Him
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read 'וַיְחַל' as related to 'חולין': משה argued that destroying Israel would be unworthy of God.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן say: It teaches that משה said before God: Master of the world! It is a profanation for You to do such a thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives yet another reading of 'וַיְחַל', this time from the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן connect 'וַיְחַל' to 'חוּלִּין', meaning something unworthy or profane. On this reading the word holds the content of משה's argument itself: wiping out Israel would not fit God's honor.

keyTerms.meaning: It is unworthy (a profanation) for You

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
It teaches that Moshe said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world!
It is a profanation for You
phrases.notes: 'חוּלִּין' sounds like 'וַיְחַל'. Here it means something that is beneath You and not fitting for You.

phrases.english: to do a thing like this.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fifth reading of 'וַיְחַל'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'וַיְחַל' means משה argued that destroying Israel would be 'חולין', unworthy of God.

steps.title: משה prayed until he was struck by אחילו
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר הגדול: משה stood in prayer until he was seized by 'אחילו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And משה beseeched before ה׳.' It was taught: רבי אליעזר הגדול says: It teaches that משה stood in prayer before God until אחילו seized him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with one more reading of 'וַיְחַל'. It uses a rare word, 'אחילו', which the next steps will explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר הגדול reads 'וַיְחַל' as related to 'אֲחִילוּ', some kind of physical suffering. This step also sets up the next two steps, because the word 'אחילו' itself needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
רבי אליעזר the Great, a תנא
A rare word for a bodily illness (explained next)

phrases.english: "And Moshe beseeched before ה׳,"
phrases.notes: שמות 32:11

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
It teaches that Moshe stood in prayer
before the Holy One, Blessed be He
until achilu seized him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הַגָּדוֹל אוֹמֵר: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁעָמַד מֹשֶׁה בִּתְפִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another reading of 'וַיְחַל', this time from a ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה prayed so intensely that he was seized by 'אחילו'.

steps.title: What is אחילו? Fire of the bones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'אחילו' means, and רבי אלעזר answers: fire of the bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is אחילו? רבי אלעזר said: fire of the bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to explain the unfamiliar word 'אחילו' from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר translates 'אחילו' into a known Hebrew phrase, 'אֵשׁ שֶׁל עֲצָמוֹת', a burning feeling in the bones. This is only the first stage of the explanation, because that phrase was not familiar to everyone either.

phrases.english: What is achilu?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵשׁ שֶׁל עֲצָמוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: Fire of the bones.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר, an אמורא. He is not רבי אליעזר הגדול from the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֲחִילוּ? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵשׁ שֶׁל עֲצָמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a word used in the ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means 'אש של עצמות', fire of the bones

steps.title: What is fire of the bones? A bone fever
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'fire of the bones' is, and אביי gives the Aramaic name of the illness: 'אשתא דגרמי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is fire of the bones? אביי said: אשתא דגרמי, a fever of the bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the explanation, turning the Hebrew phrase into the everyday Aramaic name of the illness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי identifies 'אש של עצמות' as the illness known in בבל as 'אִשָּׁתָא דְגַרְמֵי', a fever. Now the chain is complete: 'וַיְחַל' means משה prayed until he came down with a burning fever.
steps.whatToRemember: The word 'וַיְחַל' has now been read many ways: sickness, annulling a vow, giving himself over to death, mercy taking effect, 'חולין', and a bone fever. Each one shows how hard משה fought for Israel.

phrases.english: What is fire of the bones?
Abaye said: Ishta d'garmei.
phrases.notes: The same phrase in Aramaic, the everyday language in Bavel. It means a fever.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֵשׁ שֶׁל עֲצָמוֹת? אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִשָּׁתָא דְגַרְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי אלעזר's phrase from the previous step
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What illness 'אש של עצמות' refers to
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is 'אשתא דגרמי', a bone fever

steps.title: What does 'You swore to them by Yourself' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק in משה's prayer and asks what the word 'בָּךְ', 'by Yourself', means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Remember אברהם, יצחק and ישראל, Your servants, to whom You swore by Yourself.' What does 'by Yourself' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of משה's prayer and asks about one word, setting up רבי אלעזר's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'בָּךְ' seems unnecessary, because the פסוק could just say 'You swore to them'. The גמרא wants to know what argument משה was making by stressing that God swore by Himself.

phrases.english: "Remember Avraham, Yitzchak
and Yisrael, Your servants,
to whom You swore by Yourself."
phrases.notes: שמות 32:13

phrases.english: What is "by Yourself"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״בָּךְ״?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from 'וַיְחַל' to the next פסוק of משה's prayer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning and purpose of the word 'בָּךְ' in the oath

steps.title: An oath by God's eternal Name lasts forever
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that משה argued: an oath by heaven and earth could end when they end, but an oath by God's eternal Name can never be canceled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: משה said before God: Master of the world, had You sworn to them by heaven and earth, I would say that just as heaven and earth will end, so too Your oath can end. But now that You swore by Your great Name, just as Your great Name lives and lasts forever, so too Your oath lasts forever.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question about 'בָּךְ' by laying out משה's argument to God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath is only as lasting as the thing it is sworn by. Heaven and earth will someday end, so an oath tied to them could end too. God swore by His own eternal Name, so His promise to the אבות can never lapse, and Israel cannot be destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: Had (if it were the case that)

steps.whatToRemember: משה's argument: God's oath to the אבות was made 'by Himself', by His eternal Name, so it lasts forever and protects Israel forever.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the theme of these steps: משה did not only beg for mercy, he built a reasoned case from God's own promises.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Moshe said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
had You sworn to them
by the heavens and the earth,
I would say:
just as heaven and earth will cease to exist,
so too Your oath is void.
But now that You swore to them
by Your great Name,
just as Your great Name
lives and endures
forever and for all eternity,
so too Your oath endures
forever and for all eternity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, אִלְמָלֵא נִשְׁבַּעְתָּ לָהֶם בַּשָּׁמַיִם וּבָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about 'בָּךְ'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בָּךְ' means God swore by His eternal Name, so the oath lasts forever, unlike an oath by heaven and earth, which could end.

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'which I have spoken'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of משה's prayer and points out a strange word: משה says 'which I have spoken' when he should say 'which You have spoken.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And You said to them: I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens, and all this land which I have spoken of.' The גמרא asks: this phrase 'which I have spoken' should have been 'which You have spoken'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is reading the next words of משה's prayer and asks about one word that seems wrong. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה is talking to God about God's promise to the אבות. So he should say 'which You spoke,' not 'which I spoke.' The question is about who is actually speaking in this part of the פסוק.

phrases.english: "And You said to them: I will multiply your offspring
phrases.notes: שמות 32:13

phrases.english: like the stars of the heavens,
and all this land which I have spoken of."
This phrase "which I have spoken of":
it should have said "which You have spoken of"!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי אֲשֶׁר אָמַרְתִּי אֲשֶׁר אָמַרְתָּ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same פסוק whose word 'בָּךְ' was explained in Step 35.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק uses first person 'I spoke' when משה is talking about God's words.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the speaker switches from משה to God
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the פסוק changes speakers: the first part is משה talking, and the last part is God talking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Up to this point are the words of the student (משה). From this point on are the words of the Master (God).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question by saying the פסוק has two speakers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this answer the word 'I' is correct, because the words 'and all this land which I have spoken of' are said by God Himself. Nothing in the text needs to change; we just see that the speaker is different.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Up to here are the words of the student;
phrases.notes: The student is משה and the Master is God.

phrases.english: from here on are the words of the Master.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר עַד כָּאן דִּבְרֵי תַלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The end of the פסוק is God speaking, so 'I spoke' is said by God.

steps.title: רבי שמואל בר נחמני: משה says it all, about his own words
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says משה speaks the whole פסוק. 'Which I have spoken' means: I already told the Jewish people Your promise, so what do I tell them now?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: All of it is the words of the student. Rather, this is what משה said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the World, the things You told me, 'Go tell them to Israel in My name,' I went and told them in Your name. Now what can I tell them?
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer to the same question. He keeps משה as the speaker the whole time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'I' really is משה. He is saying 'the land I spoke about' because he himself delivered God's promise to the people. If God destroys them, משה is left with nothing to say to them.
steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to read 'אשר אמרתי': רבי אלעזר says God speaks the end of the פסוק; רבי שמואל בר נחמני says משה speaks it all, about the promise he passed on to ישראל.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
Both these and those are the words of the student.
Rather, this is what Moshe said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,
the things that You told me,
"Go say them to Israel in My name,"
I went and told them in Your name.
Now what can I tell them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי תַלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אלעזר in Step 37 and answers Step 36 another way.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה speaks the whole פסוק; 'which I spoke' is the promise משה himself told ישראל in God's name.

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'יכלת' instead of 'יכול'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to another prayer of משה and asks why the פסוק uses the word 'יכלת' rather than the simpler 'יכול'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Because God did not have the ability (יכלת).' It should have said: 'God was not able (יכול).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new פסוק from משה's prayer and asks about an odd choice of word. This sets up רבי אלעזר's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יכול' is the normal, masculine way to say 'able.' 'יכלת' has a feminine form. The גמרא wants to know why משה picked the feminine-sounding word.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of not having the ability

phrases.english: "Because God did not have the ability":
phrases.notes: במדבר 14:16

phrases.english: it should have said "God was not able."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִבִּלְתִּי יְכֹלֶת ה׳ יָכוֹל ה׳ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the prayer after the עגל to משה's prayer after the מרגלים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the feminine-form word 'יכלת' is used instead of 'יכול'.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the nations will say God's strength weakened
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that משה used the feminine-form word because he was telling God that the nations would say His strength had grown weak like a woman's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: משה said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the World, now the nations of the world will say His strength has weakened like a female, and He cannot save them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question about 'יכלת.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The feminine form hints at what the nations would claim: that God's power had become weak. משה uses this to argue that God should not destroy ישראל in the מדבר, because it would look like He was unable to bring them into the land.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Moshe said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,
now the nations of the world will say
His strength has weakened like a female,
and He is unable to save.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The feminine-form word shows the nations' claim that God's strength weakened like a female.

steps.title: God answers: they already saw the miracles at the sea
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא pushes back on משה: the nations already saw the miracles God did at the sea, so how could they say He is weak?
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to משה: But didn't they already see the miracles and mighty acts that I did for them at the sea?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the story, God challenges משה's argument. This sets up משה's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God's point is that the nations already know His power from קריעת ים סוף. So the claim 'He is too weak to save' should not be believable.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moshe:
But didn't they already see
the miracles and mighty acts that I did for them
at the sea?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר רָאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges משה's claim from Step 40.
steps.kashyaTarget: משה's claim that the nations will say God is too weak to save.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The nations already saw God's great power at the sea, so they cannot call Him weak.

steps.title: משה replies: one king is not thirty-one kings
steps.stepSummary: משה answers that the nations can still say God could beat one king (פרעה) but cannot beat the thirty-one kings of כנען.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה said before Him: Master of the World, they can still say: He can stand up against one king, but He cannot stand up against thirty-one kings.
steps.whatsHappening: משה answers God's challenge and keeps his argument alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The miracles at the sea were against only one king, פרעה. The nations could claim that conquering ארץ ישראל, with its thirty-one kings, is too much. So destroying ישראל in the מדבר would still look like weakness.
steps.whatToRemember: משה's argument: even after the sea, the nations could say God beat one king but cannot beat the thirty-one kings of כנען, so ישראל must not be destroyed.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the World,
they can still say:
Against one king He can stand,
phrases.notes: The one king is פרעה.

phrases.aramaic: לִשְׁלשִׁים וְאֶחָד מְלָכִים אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַעֲמוֹד.
phrases.english: against thirty-one kings He cannot stand.
phrases.notes: These are the kings of כנען that ישראל would later fight (יהושע 12:24).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם עֲדַיִין יֵשׁ לָהֶם לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers God's challenge in Step 41.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between defeating one king and defeating many kings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The miracles at the sea already proved God's power to the nations.
steps.terutzMaskana: Beating one king does not prove, in the nations' eyes, that God can beat thirty-one kings.

steps.title: God agreed with משה in the end
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a פסוק showing that הקדוש ברוך הוא accepted משה's argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: How do we know that הקדוש ברוך הוא came around and agreed with משה? Because the פסוק says, 'And ה׳ said: I have forgiven, according to your words.'
steps.whatsHappening: After משה's argument about the nations (step 42), רבי יוחנן shows that God accepted it. The proof is the words 'according to your words.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: God had pushed back on משה (step 41), and משה answered (step 42). The word 'כדבריך' shows that God forgave because of what משה said, which means He agreed with משה's argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Turned back, came around to a new position
Agreed with him, conceded to him

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, came around
and agreed with Moshe?
As it is said: "And ה׳ said:
I have forgiven, according to your words."
phrases.notes: במדבר 14:20. The proof is in the word 'according to your words': God forgave because of משה's argument.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי יוחנן: מנין שחזר הקדוש ברוך הוא והודה לו למשה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the outcome of the back-and-forth in steps 41-42: God accepted משה's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'סלחתי כדבריך' show that God agreed with משה's argument.

steps.title: The nations really would have said it
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל explains 'כדבריך' to mean that משה was right about what the nations would say.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'According to your words' means that the nations of the world will one day say exactly that.
steps.whatsHappening: A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל explains what 'according to your words' means. God is telling משה that his warning was correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 42 משה warned that the nations would say God could defeat one king but not thirty-one. Here God agrees that the nations would in fact say this, so משה's claim was true.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught
Will in the future, are going to

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"According to your words":
the nations of the world will one day say so.
phrases.notes: God is saying משה was right: the nations really would say what he warned about in step 42.

steps.triggerLanguage: תני דבי רבי ישמעאל: כדבריך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains more about the word 'כדבריך' that רבי יוחנן used as his proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'כדבריך' means that משה's warning about the nations was correct.

steps.title: Fortunate is the student whose teacher agrees with him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a lesson: it is a great thing when a teacher agrees with his student.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fortunate is the student whose teacher agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the story with a short lesson. God, the 'teacher,' agreed with משה, the 'student.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה is God's student, yet God accepted his argument. The גמרא calls a student fortunate when this happens, because his teacher's agreement shows that his reasoning was correct.
steps.whatToRemember: The story of משה's prayer after the spies ends with God agreeing with משה: 'סלחתי כדבריך.' Fortunate is the student whose teacher agrees with him.

phrases.english: Fortunate is the student
whose teacher agrees with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אשרי תלמיד שרבו מודה לו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the closing lesson from God agreeing with משה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A student is fortunate when his teacher agrees with him, as God agreed with משה.

steps.title: You gave Me life with your words
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of רב יצחק reads 'חי אני' as God telling משה that his words gave Him life.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the פסוק 'But indeed, as I live,' רבא said in the name of רב יצחק: This teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא said to משה, 'משה, you have given Me life with your words.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next פסוק after 'סלחתי כדבריך.' רב יצחק reads 'as I live' as God saying that משה's words gave Him life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally 'חי אני' is an oath, 'as I live.' רב יצחק reads it as 'I live through your words,' showing how pleased God was that משה's arguments led Him to forgive.

keyTerms.meaning: As I live (here read as: I am alive)

phrases.english: "But indeed, as I live":
phrases.notes: במדבר 14:21, the פסוק right after 'סלחתי כדבריך.'

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moshe:
Moshe, you have given Me life with your words.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואולם חי אני, אמר רבא אמר רב יצחק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק and adds another sign of God's approval of משה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'חי אני' teaches that God told משה, 'You have given Me life with your words.'

steps.title: Praise God first, then pray
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי teaches that a person should always praise הקדוש ברוך הוא before praying for his own needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמלאי expounded: A person should always first set out the praise of הקדוש ברוך הוא, and only afterward pray for what he needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic about the right order of prayer. רבי שמלאי says praise comes first and requests come after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a practical rule about how to pray. You do not open with your own requests. First you praise God, and only then you ask.

keyTerms.meaning: Should set out, arrange in order

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains the order of שמונה עשרה, which opens with blessings of praise before the middle blessings of requests.

steps.title: משה praised God before asking to enter the land
steps.stepSummary: The source is משה's prayer in ספר דברים: first he praised God's greatness, and only afterward he asked to cross into ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it from משה. It is written, 'And I pleaded with ה׳ at that time.' Then it is written, 'ה׳ God, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your strong hand, for who is a god in heaven or on earth who can do deeds and mighty acts like Yours?' Only after that is it written, 'Please let me cross over and see the good land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the order of פסוקים in משה's prayer. Praise comes first, and the personal request comes after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the sequence. After 'ואתחנן' משה does not ask right away. He first praises God (פסוק 24) and only then makes his request (פסוק 25). This matches רבי שמלאי's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמלאי: praise God first, then ask. The proof is משה, who praised God's greatness before asking to enter ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: A memory list for the coming teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, a list of seven key words, to help remember the series of teachings that comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: A memory aid: Deeds, charity, offering, priest, fast, shoe, iron.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is not teaching a rule here. It is setting up the next section by listing one key word from each upcoming teaching so you can keep them in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סימן works like a table of contents. Each word, such as קרבן or תענית, points to a teaching that will use that word. When you reach each teaching, match it to its word in this list.
